scripts.//test: THE CEILING IS NO LONGER ON THIS LINE — it is scripts/test-ceiling.mjs, preloaded from bunfig.toml (#740), and that file records what was measured. It was `--timeout 20000` here, because `[test] timeout` is not a bunfig.toml key and bun ignores unknown keys silently (#414 shipped exactly that, and this suite — a real daemon, a worker and child processes per test — ran on bun's 5 s default for every day it was believed fixed). The cost of a flag was that it only applies to the command carrying it: `bun test apps/engine/test/one.test.ts` from the repo root got 5 s while CI got 20, and four failures were relayed as machine contention on durations that were exactly a default ceiling. A flag here would now be redundant rather than wrong: the preload reads an explicit `--timeout` back off the operating system and stands aside for it, so one typed on the command line still wins in either direction, and `TELAR_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=N` covers a run that cannot pass one. A test's own third-argument ceiling beats both. The `eventually`/`until` helpers in test/*.test.ts carry the matching 15 s wall-clock bound, so a wait can outlast a loaded runner without outlasting this ceiling.
